picks.title: Parshas Nitzavim & Vayeilech (Rebroadcast)
picks.summary: On the final day of Moshe’s life, he gathered the entire nation – men, women, children, and according to the Talmud, all souls of future Jews – to pass them through a final covenant with God. The parsha also contains the prophetic predictions of the Messianic times, and it ends with a simple, binary choice: Moshe tells the nation, “Behold I have placed before you today, the life and the good, and death and evil… Choose Life!” Moshe is 120 years old to the day. picks.reason: Detailed teaching on Moshe's final day and the covenant to choose life.

picks.showTitle: Nitzotzos: Inspiration to Keep Your Spark Alive with Rav Mordechai Burg
picks.title: Nitzavim - You Don’t Need to Become More Jewish. You Need to Become More Yourself.
picks.summary: Most of us assume that Yiddishkeit is something being asked of us from the outside. And when it feels difficult, we take that difficulty as proof that it is not really who we are.But the Torah says something very different: “Ki karov eilecha hadavar me’od”—it is already exceedingly close, in your mouth and in your heart.In this shiur, delivered in Tomer Devorah, Rav Burg explores the startling idea that Torah is not foreign to the Jewish soul. It may become buried beneath habit, shame, or the noise of the yetzer hara, but buried is not gone. Drawing on the Rambam, Tanya, Maharal, Rav Tzadok, a
picks.reason: Explores Torah's closeness to the self and Jewish spiritual identity deeply.

picks.title: Rabbi Gordon - Nitzavim-Vayelech: 6th Portion
picks.summary: These classes teach the day’s section of the weekly Torah portion. The lesson is taught using the original Hebrew text with the indispensable commentary of Rashi—both translated and elucidated so that anyone can follow along.
picks.reason: Detailed study of weekly Torah portion with Rashi commentary for spiritual and ethical insight.

picks.title: Parsha: Nitzavim & Vayeilech - Mavericks vs. Heat
picks.summary: The entire book of Devarim occurs over the span of 36 days, the final 36 days of Moshe's life. The final four Parshas are an account of the last day of Moshe's life. As he is about to transition to the other world, the reliable shepherd gathers all the people together for one last covenant and exhortation to hearken to the word of God and to not go astray. But why would the nation go astray? These are the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who were chosen by God to be his people. This is the nation that witnessed the Exodus, the theophany at Sinai, who ate the manna and drank water from
picks.reason: Reflection on Moses' final days and covenant with Israel on faithfulness and ethics.

picks.title: IKAR High Holy Days Bootcamp 5787
picks.summary: Grab a glass of grape juice or wine and a comfy chair, and join your rabbis for a launch of the season. We’ll cover many of the High Holy Day basics (What can I expect if I’m coming for the first time? Wait, another Amidah? And which service do I wear white to?), along with some of the most perplexing questions of the season (Remind me why we’re doing all this? Why does September feel like a marathon? Is teshuvah really possible?). We’ll do our best to connect, elucidate, and elaborate in 90 minutes or less.
picks.reason: High Holy Days basics and deep questions about teshuvah and meaning.

picks.title: Episode 551: Elul 2026 IV - Nitzavim (Standing at Sinai) - Lex and Wendie
picks.summary: Elul is the 12th and final month of the Jewish calendar year. Elul Unbound is a Judaism Unbound initiative all about making Elul meaningful, through creative digital modalities. In this conversation, Lex Rofeberg and Wendie Bernstein Lash ask what the Torah portion Nitzavim (from Deuteronomy, meaning "standing") can teach us about what it means to gather en masse -- with other Jews on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, or as a broader community beyond just Jews. This Elul episode is the fourth and final conversation in a series of four episodes being released as part of Elul Unbound 2026.----------
picks.reason: A reflective conversation on communal meaning in the Torah portion Nitzavim.

picks.title: God
picks.summary: During Passover, two rabbis discuss how the holiday can be both reflective and joyful, aiming to disrupt routine rather than induce suffering. In a “Day in the Life of a Rabbi” segment, one recounts a challenging Hebrew school class interrupted by a student obsessed with shouting “Very nice,” including a reveal from a closet, while the other admits to mocking a teacher’s name as a child and reflects on how Hebrew school behavior doesn’t predict adulthood. picks.reason: Two rabbis discuss Passover's meaning and reflections on God and childhood.

picks.title: Rambam: Ishut, Chapter 8
picks.summary: Rabbi Gordon studies one chapter a day from Maimonides’ classic legal work of Mishneh Torah. The original Hebrew text is read and then translated and clearly explained in English.
picks.reason: Careful study of Maimonides' legal text illuminating Jewish law and ethics.

picks.title: Michael Weingrad on Contemporary Israeli Poetry
picks.summary: Man is a storytelling animal, and conveying the experience of the human condition in poetry and prose helps us understand and contend with it. That's true in all times and places, and it is why students of a society and its culture have much to learn from its poets. Contemporary Israel is one of the most interesting societies anywhere on earth, and its poets encompass the depth of its culture—God and man, the inescapability of war, human vices large and small. picks.reason: Explores Israeli poetry's engagement with human condition and Jewish culture.

picks.title: Where Have You Gone Mussar Movement?
picks.summary:
What happened to the Mussar Movement following its near decimation in the Holocaust? Were there attempts to reestablish it? Were those attempts successful? If not, why not? If yes, how can that limited success be measured? How broad in scope was the success of the Mussar Movement even prior to its destruction in the Holocaust? A Mussar Movement history episode in honor of Elul.
